subject.title: Question: Publisher verification path for active code plugin contributors?

question: Should ClawHub define a public verified or vetted-community path for third-party code-plugin publishers, and should that status be package-scoped, publisher-scoped, or unavailable for now?
rationale: Current main has official/community/private, source-linked verification, trustedPublisher, and exact-release scan surfaces, but none of those answer whether community executable-plugin publishers can receive an endorsement-like trust signal.

options.title: Use the RFC as the policy owner
options.body: Keep this author-specific issue as context, and settle criteria, scope, revocation, wording, and implementation sequencing in https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/issues/2272 before coding status changes.

options.title: Document no community verified path
options.body: State that Official remains staff-assigned only and community plugins rely on source-linked, provenance, scan, and moderation evidence rather than a separate verified path.

options.title: Pilot a vetted-community program
options.body: Approve a limited package or publisher pilot with explicit review requirements, expiry, revocation, admin workflow, API fields, and UI wording.

recommendation.title: Use the RFC as the policy owner
recommendation.body: Keep this author-specific issue as context, and settle criteria, scope, revocation, wording, and implementation sequencing in https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/issues/2272 before coding status changes.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick is the strongest current-history owner for official-publisher policy, package trust schema, and the plugin trust API surface.
